jira_comment:
Validated deploy-ready against a throwaway instance built from 2cd9104ea, using the demo and mayo tenants.

Positive: a case staged with an EVAL_FOR_ERAS procedure and then left looking like an HL7-scheduled case (no start time, flag unset) came back erasOperation=true from app launch, and firing ERAS_OPERATION_END recorded a-eras-antiemetics as fired. This held for a non-hysterectomy procedure, which is the point of the ticket. The shipped mayo procedure list carries the tag on 70 procedures, and cases built on the real tags (colectomy, knee arthroplasty, spinal fusion) all came back on the protocol; one tagged procedure among several is enough.

Negative: a case carrying an untagged procedure came back erasOperation=false and a-eras-antiemetics recorded not-fired with "Not ERAS operation.". The once-only guard was checked both ways on started cases: a case already on the protocol whose procedure changed to an untagged one stayed on it, and a case already off it whose procedure changed to a tagged one stayed off.

Red check: the pre-fix version of OperationService was compiled and swapped into the running container. With it in place, the same scheduled hysterectomy case launched with erasOperation=false and the ERAS alert did not fire. The shipped class was then restored, checksum verified against the backup, and the identical case re-run - erasOperation=true and the alert fired.

Caveats: Mayo's real Epic-driven case start could not be driven locally, so mayo was covered through the admin create-operation endpoint on the shipped tags while the launch path was exercised on demo.

Automation: the Java unit coverage added with the change already covers the scheduled-case, no-other-change and leave-alone-once-started paths. Worth adding are the inverse leave-alone case (a started non-ERAS case that gains a tagged procedure), coverage of the admin create-operation endpoint setting the flag, and a multi-procedure case where only one procedure carries the tag. No qa-suite work is warranted - the only ERAS spec there is a skipped placeholder for a rule the app ignores.
